title: Commander Order
description: One commander order (CO): the pilot's conduct and behaviour for the session, held in the commander's own words, verbatim. Promotion to a standing order (SO) if it turns out to be universal conduct across any session is its own separate record, not a flag here; the promoted CO becomes superseded and is never pruned. A CO that is instead satisfied or no longer applicable is retired and eventually pruned. Every CO is answered by a pilot decision (XD). Filed by identifier with a dash, CO-012.json.
x-expect: exactly one of statement (one verbatim span) or statements (a bracketed list of verbatim spans, for a record drawn from two or more non-adjacent places) is present

kind.description: the word commander-order, which is what chooses this schema

id.description: this order's identifier, CO, a dash and three digits, the same identifier the file is named for

name.description: one to three words the writer chose for the record's contents, appended to the file name after the id (CA-049)

date.description: the day the commander said it, YYYY-MM-DD

session.description: the eight-character id of the session the order was given in

status.description: whether the order stands: active while it governs conduct, retired once satisfied or no longer applicable, superseded once promoted to a standing order (SO) — a promoted CO is never pruned, superseded_by keeps pointing at the SO

answered_by.description: the pilot decision that answers this order, carried on both the CO record and its manifest row; absent until a decision is written

binds.description: who the order binds: pilot (the default, and assumed when absent) for the pilot's own conduct, all for conduct that binds every agent in the cockpit

summary.description: a plain-language summary of the whole order, simple words with no jargon; only this text goes to the manifest

statement.description: the commander's own words, verbatim and never edited; present when the order is drawn from one span of the constitution or transcript. Exactly one of statement or statements is present, never both

statements.description: the commander's own words, verbatim and never edited, as a bracketed list of two or more spans, used in place of statement when the order is stated in two or more non-adjacent places, such as two separate lines of the constitution with an unrelated sentence between them. Each entry is one contiguous span in document order; the spans are never joined into one string, since that would read as continuous prose and stop being verbatim

lines.description: the constitution line or lines this order is sourced from, a string such as "8", "31-32", "58-63" or "3, 52, 54", so the statement can be checked against the document in one step; present for a record sourced from the constitution, absent for one given in chat

brief.description: the surrounding transcript context: what prompted the order and what it applies to

superseded_by.description: the identifier of the later order that overrides this one, or the standing order it was promoted into; absent while the order stands

superseded_note.description: how and why it was superseded, in prose, when the identifier alone does not tell the story

note.description: a short note by the commander or the pilot on the record's status, such as why it was retired
